This letter is being written to outline the Air Quality-Asbestos Program requirements and
recommendations in regard to the burned material remaining at thesite of theformer Hitching Post Inn
located at 170o w Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY.This letteris divided into two sections in regard to the
material remaining.
Intact/Partially-Damaged/Standing-but-Unsafe-to-Enter Portions
These areas of the sitefall under all the requirements of the Asbestos NE SHAP regulation.This
regulation requires thorough inspections or assumption of all suspect material aspositive priorto
renovation or demolition, notification to the Division10working-days prior to the start of any activity to
work area, and the use of trained personnel to perform the activity.The waste material from these
portions of the site must be disposed of ina landfill that will accept Regulated Asbestos Containing
posted on each container.A general waste manifest wouldneed to accompany the waste from the
project site to the chosen landfill.
Theimpact of this regulation may be minimized in areas of the building that are demolished under an
order of a State of local government agency because the facility is structurally unsound and indangerof
imminent collapse.
The Division would be willing to waive some, if not all, of the10-working days of advance notice for this
project and would considered it an emergency project.A copy of the notification form and a set of
instructions to facilitate form completion are enclosed for your convenience.The State of Wyoming
doesnothave a registration or li censure program for Building Inspectors/Contractors, sowecannot
provide a list of entities that canperform this work.Wenormally suggest that facility owners examine
the local phone booksection on“Environmental and Ecological Services”or"Asbestos Abatement";
examine regulatory programs from surrounding states; or ask for references from local contractors.
